newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: National Mutual NZ stays overweight in NZ shares.
newsitem.headline: National Mutual NZ stays overweight in NZ shares.

text.p: National Mutual Funds Management New Zealand Ltd (NMFM) said on Tuesday that domestic shares had proved the star performer in the December quarter and were showing potential for further growth.

"We have maintained the overweight position in New Zealand shares at 60 to 65 percent through the allocation range because we continue to see value in the market and further upside on a 12-month view," NMFM said.
It said its shares sector returned 12.2 percent before tax over the December quarter, while the NZSE-40 Gross Index gained 10.1 percent.
Balanced or diversified superannuation funds under NMFM's management returned 6.2 percent to 6.6 percent before tax.

"These quarterly results reflected the strong contribution made by the New Zealand share sector as well as the decision to remain overweighted in the sector over the quarter," chief investment officer Barry Lindsay said.
"The other asset classes achieved positive results with lower long-term interest rates generating capital gains for both the New Zealand and international fixed interest sectors."

Lindsay said diversified funds under NMFM's discretionary management achieved returns ranging from 11.9 percent to 12.9 percent in the 1996 calendar year, following strong returns in 1995 between 17.1 percent and 18.4 percent.

He said NMFM had adopted a slightly more conservative stance in early December given the strength of the rally in the domestic and international bond markets. It cut exposures back to underweight for domestic bonds and neutral for international bonds, redirecting those funds into cash.
"We basically felt risk premiums available from bonds had shrunk too far," Lindsay said.

He said NMFM had concerns about the ability of the U.S. equity market to keep rising at such a pace, and had not enjoyed seeing Japan in "almost freefall" over the last week. NMFM was underweight in both U.S. and Japanese equity markets.

During the December quarter NMFM began accepting investments into its new NMFM Super 10 Fund which, like the Stock Exchange's TeNZ fund, is indexed to the NZSE 10 Capital Index. The fund has been established as a superannuation fund in its own right.
